scope: Actual signed hardened macOS ARM64 protocol-2 application lifecycle at the pinned revisions; not universal or Intel or final-toolchain certification.

runtime.label: before-expiry-pro-e10
runtime.note: Expiry-test launch began three seconds before deadline; actual valid-lease pro report reconciled after validator timeout. This does not establish expired-lease behavior.

runtime.label: replay-api-policy-attempt-e10
runtime.note: Initial harness incorrectly expected thrown check error; API returns upToDate on rejected response. Actual free fallback/report and data reconciled. Dedicated request/evidence capture rerun required.

tamper_controls.isolation: Restore only owned cache artifact/state/pointers between independent tamper controls; this is test reset, not automatic repair. Selection journal and application data are never restored.

response_replay.scope: Real signed previously accepted response replayed over HTTP; old request nonce also differs, so this proves response replay rejection, not isolated epoch-only rejection.

ffi.limits: Per-launch FFI files were validated live but overwritten in the app container; the final free raw verification is retained. Native exports came only from the original signed app.

limitations: One expiry-test attempt started three seconds before its deadline and correctly ran pro; reconciled separately, then a fresh post-expiry cold launch passed.

The first replay validator expected an exception; the public bool check API instead reported upToDate with unchanged authority. Reconciled separately and reran with captured requests and unchanged journal.
Replayed response also had an old nonce; isolated epoch-only rejection remains unit-test evidence.
Tamper controls restored owned cache bytes between isolated tests; that restoration is not automatic repair.
OS-owned container metadata shell remains EPERM; app payload, all variant Keychain keys, bootstrap secrets and owned API processes were removed.
The newly integrated macOS x64/native toolchain requires its own fresh builds and runtime validation.
